name: Per-model review state and collision check

pr.title: Give each reviewing model its own state, lock, and collision check
pr.head: 808a0e922524ba9c5184f389225b6d2096a967a5

summary: project review is the CLI that a review loop uses to set up, publish, and clean up each review of a pull request. Until now it took the GitHub account as the reviewer. So when two review loops ran different models on one pull request under one account, such as one in Claude Code and one in Codex, they got in each other's way. The second model's setup refused on the first model's lock. Once that lock was released, the second setup overwrote the first model's state file and could remove a scratch worktree the first model was still reading. Its publish then refused on the first model's verdict as if another loop had posted it.
This pull request is one layer of the multi-model review plan (docs/projects/multi-model-review/readme.md). It makes the model the reviewer's identity within an account, and it changes three things:

1. Local state per model. Each model's state, lock, request file, and worktree live under a folder named after the model. Every command after setup finds its review by the pull request and --model, or by the only model set up on the machine.
  2. A duplicate caught at setup. setup lists the reviewer's start comments and refuses while another session's live start comment names the same model.
  3. A per-model collision check. publish counts only verdicts by this model, or by no model, as earlier releases wrote them.

The layers above this one add the sign-off rule, census --wait, status, and adoption of a stopped model's findings. Until they land, the last publish still sets the draft state, and each model still settles every finding. This pull request is stacked on #233, which shows each model's verdict in a summary's header.

cards.title: Terms
cards.html:
• Identity: the model ID lowercased, with any trailing bracketed variant removed, so claude-opus-5-5[1m] and Claude-Opus-5-5 are both claude-opus-5-5.
  • Model key: the identity with every character other than a letter, a digit, ., _, or - replaced by -. It names the folder that holds a model's state.
  • Start comment: the comment setup posts to announce a review in progress. publish deletes it.
  • Live: a start comment is live until its model posts a verdict on its head after it, or a day passes since its last edit.
  • Loop record: loops/<id>/published.json, the list of reviews a loop published.

cards.title: Review so far
cards.html:
• The first review, at 28e3f69, requested changes on one finding. start-review-loop told the loop to pass --model to every project review command, but review census rejected the flag.
  • 3bb9ba7 adds --model to census and lists the seven commands that take the loop's flags in both skills. The second review found that head clean, and 653 tests passed.
  • 808a0e9 rebases both commits unchanged onto #233 after #233 merged main, and rewraps a docstring that merge left with an overlong line. The third review found it clean, and 701 tests passed.

groups.title: Per-model identity, state, and collision in review.py
groups.kicker: Where each model's review lives, how setup spots a duplicate, and what publish counts as a collision
intro: All of the behavior is in src/projector/review.py. identity(), which an earlier layer added, decides when two model IDs name the same reviewer. model_key() turns that identity into a safe folder name. Paths now takes the model and puts the state, lock, request, and worktree paths under that key.

The state file records its identity, so two IDs that make the same key, such as a/b and a-b, refuse rather than share a folder. setup reads the account's start comments and reviews before it posts, and refuses when a live start comment by the same model is not the one this machine recorded. When this machine recorded one that was never published, setup deletes it after posting the new one. check_collision now ignores verdicts by other models.

checks.text: No state from the old layout is read. A review that was set up before an upgrade runs setup again, as the plan's § 3 decides.

files.note: Model key, per-model Paths, model lookup for later commands, the start-comment duplicate check, and the per-model collision check.

checks.text: model_key refuses an empty ID, whitespace, a bare variant such as [1m], .., and a key that starts with .. It turns / into -, so no ID can name a path outside the state directory. I traced it and checked the test cases in test_setup_refuses_a_model_id_no_folder_can_be_made_from.
stored_state refuses when the folder's state has another identity. setup calls it before it takes the lock, so a key that two identities share refuses before anything is posted.

is_live ends a start comment's life only on a verdict by the same identity on the comment's SHA, submitted at or after the comment's creation. A re-review's start comment stays live after the verdict that came before it. move edits the comment, which refreshes the day-long window. I traced both paths.

Without --model, find_model returns the only model with a state.json for this pull request, and refuses when there are several. A lock left with no state file, from a setup killed partway, needs release --model.
setup deletes the start comment it recorded earlier only after the new comment posts, and only when that comment is still on the pull request. A refused setup deletes nothing and releases its lock.
same_model reads model= from the loose marker line instead of verdict_marker, so a marker in an older shape still collides. A marker with no model= collides with every model.

Each loop-record entry now names its model. The incremental rules from #228 do not filter by it. They can only refuse when two models share one loop id, because the full review's marker must name this run's model.

groups.title: The --model flag on later commands
intro: src/projector/cli.py adds an optional --model to move, census, release, publish, gate, and interdiff. All but census resolve the review's paths through review_paths. census reads every model's threads from GitHub, so it only checks that the ID is usable, which lets a loop pass the same flags to each command. release moves ahead of the path lookup, so with no review set up it reports zero locks instead of refusing.

files.note: Adds --model to six review subcommands. Five find the review through review_paths, and census only checks the ID.

checks.text: census is now in this list. I parsed setup, move, census, interdiff, gate, publish, and release with --loop and --model using this head's parser, and all seven accept both flags. census checks the ID with model_key and still counts every model's threads.

groups.title: The review skills
groups.kicker: How review-pr and start-review-loop describe one model among several
intro: review-pr gains a section on reviewing as one model among several. It also documents the model= field on the start, finding, and verify markers, the per-model lock, and the per-model collision check. start-review-loop gives each model's loop its own id, such as <repo>-review-<model-key>, finds the last reviewed head from this model's verdicts, and passes --model.

The plan gets two corrections that match what was built: setup deletes the start comment it recorded and never published, and each setup adds two listings, not one. The plan stays in-progress, because the layers above still have to land.

groups.title: Tests
groups.kicker: ModelTests and the existing suites moved to the per-model layout
intro: ModelTests runs against the fake GitHub in temporary repositories. It covers two models on one head, a missing --model, start comments that are live, stale, or from an earlier release, the collision rule across ID variants, unusable IDs, and a key that two identities share. A new test reads the command list from start-review-loop and runs each command with --loop and --model. The existing setup, publish, and incremental tests now read state from the model's folder.
